title: TDD with an agent: a pricing-rules module
goal: Step 1: read RULES.md in the project and write the tests yourself in tests/pricing.test.js (cover every rule, both sides of each boundary, invalid input and the empty order). Step 2: run npm run lock-tests and commit. Step 3: have the agent implement src/pricing.js with the tests protected, using the starting prompt. Step 4: npm run verify fails if any test file changed since it was locked.
setup_cmd: D=~/fm-ex/ex-3-2-tdd; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo "Already set up at $D. Run: cd $D (or delete it first to start over)."; else mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-3-2-tdd/starter "$D" && cd "$D" && git init -q -b main && git add -A && git -c user.name=fm -c user.email=fm@example.com commit -qm baseline && npm install; fi

starter_prompts.claude: Start Claude Code with the tests protected: claude --settings '{"permissions":{"deny":["Edit(tests/**)"]}}'. Then paste: Implement src/pricing.js so that npm test passes, following RULES.md. The tests in tests/ are the contract: do not edit, delete, skip or rename any of them. If you believe a test is wrong, stop and explain which assertion and why; do not change it. Run npm test after each change and report the final output.
starter_prompts.codex: Add "Never modify files under tests/. If a test looks wrong, stop and explain." to AGENTS.md, then start codex and paste: Implement src/pricing.js so that npm test passes, following RULES.md. The tests in tests/ are the contract: do not edit, delete, skip or rename any of them. If a test looks wrong, stop and explain which assertion and why instead of changing it. Run npm test after each change and report the final output.

solution_notes: The tests are written and locked before implementation exists. The reference tests name each rule (subtotal, volume, gold, coupon, shipping, vat, empty, invalid) and pin every boundary: qty 9/10/49/50, coupon net 1999/2000, shipping net 4999/5000.

The order of operations is fixed by tests, not by the implementation: volume discount, then gold tier, then the coupon threshold check, then shipping on the discounted net, then VAT on net excluding shipping.
All money is integer cents and every percentage goes through one helper that rounds half up, which avoids floating-point drift.
npm run verify passes only if tests.lock still matches the files under tests/. The guard is a script outside the agent, so it holds even when a deny rule or an instruction is bypassed.
